title: Hosted API offline replay and tool snapshot playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc collects design proposals and implementation notes for enabling robust offline replay and compact tool snapshots for the Hosted API. The goal is to let clients (mobile, edge, server) capture enough structured state from an in-progress streaming session (including tool calls and partial structured output) to: (a) replay locally when network is intermittent, (b) resume against server for continuity, and (c) support deterministic QA / fuzzy-eval loops without re-running full model compute.

Background / motivation:
- We have many hosted streaming flows where partial structured output + tool integrations are emitted over the wire. Currently if a client disconnects or loses network mid-stream, there is either (i) an expensive server-side session resume (re-run expensive model compute) or (ii) opaque client-side heuristics that lead to duplication and poor UX.
- Problems we want to solve: minimizing re-UGPU cost on resume, predictable semantics for tool side-effects, reproducible local replays for debugging and eval, and an ergonomic SDK surface for snapshotting and replay.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: full transactional guarantees across arbitrary external tools. We will provide strong idempotency and reconciliation guidance, but not distributed transactions.
- Constraint: snapshots must be compact for mobile (target < 50KB typical, 200KB worst-case). Avoid heavyweight binary blobs.
- Constraint: sensitive data redaction must be enforced at capture time and be auditable.

Key concepts / glossary (short):
- Snapshot: compact, serialized capture of session state at a stream checkpoint.
- Checkpoint: a deterministic boundary in the stream where the SDK may request a snapshot (e.g., end of a tool call, after N tokens of stable JSON).
- Replay: local or server-side process that consumes a snapshot and attempts to reconstruct an equivalent session state to continue the conversation or re-run evaluation.
- Deterministic hydration: ability to reconstitute argument objects, tool results, and partial outputs such that downstream app code can make consistent decisions without re-running the model.

Proposed snapshot schema (high-level):
- Version header (v1): minimal metadata (model variant, sequence id, snapshot id, timestamp, server protocol version)
- Checkpoint markers: list of stable frame ids + offsets
- Token prefix hash: small rolling-hash for quick integrity checks (not a crypto signature)
- Structured frames: a small array of typed frames (type: message/tool-call/attachment), each containing: frame_type, stable_id, timestamp, actor, compact-payload (see framing rules)
- Tool outputs: canonicalized tool responses, accompanied by tool-metadata (tool-id, tool-version, idempotency-key, canonical-result-hash)
- Application hints: optional user-provided hints (redaction flags, fields to omit, preferred reconcile policy)
- SDK telemetry mask: set of flags that indicate what telemetry is allowed to be captured (helps privacy/compliance)

Framing rules (compact-payload):
- Use newline-delimited JSON with small shorthand keys where possible to keep size down. Example payload: {"t":"msg","m":"Summarize the API","s":true}
- Binary attachments (images, audio) are not embedded; instead include a stable storage id + small preview metadata.
- Canonicalization: tool outputs must be normalized (sorted keys where deterministic, standardized timestamps, remove transient_ids).

SDK ergonomics: API surface (draft):
- Snapshot.create(checkpointReason: string, options?: {redact?: string[], telemetryMask?: string[]}) -> Promise<SnapshotHandle>
  - creates snapshot on client request; returns handle containing size estimate and signed snapshot id for later upload/resume.
- Snapshot.export(handle, mode: "compact" | "verbose") -> Buffer / string
  - compact mode for mobile upload; verbose for server-side debugging.
- Replay.consume(snapshot, policy: "client-local" | "server-resume" | "dry-run") -> ReplayResult
  - dry-run validates snapshot integrity and reports reconciliation conflicts without executing tool side-effects.
- Tool integration primitives: Tool.register({id, version, idempotencyKeyFn}) and Tool.reconcile(snapshotEntry, policy) -> reconcileReport
  - encourages tool authors to provide pure result hashes and small reconcile hooks.

Behavioral rules and semantics (high level):
- Checkpoint consistency: server will only label a frame checkpoint when model output for previous frame is stable (heuristic: JSON parseable + schema-valid or end-of-tool-call).
- Tool-side effects: by default, tool calls are recorded as "intent + canonical result" pairs. On replay with server-resume, the platform will attempt to reconcile by comparing canonical-result-hash; if mismatch, options: accept server canonical result, present conflict to client, or re-run tool if idempotency key allows.
- Idempotency keys: tool authors must support idempotency keys for operations that mutate external state; SDK will generate or accept developer-provided keys.

Offline flows (examples):
1) Mobile intermittent network resume (common):
   - Client captures snapshot after tool call complete (checkpoint).
   - Network dies. Client opens offline UI; user edits the latest partial structured output locally.
   - On reconnect, client calls Replay.consume(snapshot, "server-resume"). Server validates token-prefix-hash, accepts snapshot if within TTL (default 10 minutes for low-latency flows), and attempts to reconcile tool outputs. If a tool's canonical-result-hash differs, server returns a conflict response and suggests reconcile actions.
2) Local QA replay for regression testing:
   - Engineering exports verbose snapshot for a session and checks into an evaluation bucket. Offline test harness runs local deterministic hydration and compares generated final outputs against baseline.
3) Edge caching with speculative prefetch:
   - Edge SDK stores snapshots for active sessions for 30s; when new partial requests arrive for same session id, edge can serve a speculative local resume to hide tail latency while server reconciles in background.

Operational concerns and telemetry:
- Telemetry: Snapshot.create must emit small telemetry: snapshot_size_bytes, frames_count, tool_frame_count, redact_flags_used. Telemetry must be opt-in for PII-sensitive teams.
- Storage and retention: snapshots uploaded to Redwood should be TTL'd by default (30 days for logs, 24 hours for low-latency ephemeral snapshots), with enterprise controls to reduce retention or enforce encryption-at-rest with customer KMS.
- Security: snapshots must enforce at-capture redaction policy. SDK will run a best-effort local redaction pass and tag fields that couldn't be redacted for server-side review.

Edge cases and open questions (brainstorm fragments):
- How to handle long-running tool calls that produce streaming progress updates (partial results) and then a final result? We could capture intermediate frames but only mark checkpoint at final result. But that loses ability to resume to an intermediate point. Tradeoffs.
- TTL policy: 10 minutes feels OK for interactive apps but enterprise workflows (long forms) might need hours. Add server-side policy configurable per route.
- Conflict UX: present a diff view? automatic merge heuristics? For structured JSON, we could attempt three-way merge using canonical-result hashes as anchors.
- Binary payload indexing: should we store blobs in object-store referenced by snapshot id or embed small base64 previews? Prefer object-store; cost/latency tradeoff.
- Snapshot signing: do we need cryptographic signing for cross-region resume? For now, use HMAC with account key for authenticity.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment): lightweight client snapshot export + server dry-run validation. No automatic resume. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (resume prototype): server-side resume endpoint that accepts compact snapshots, validates integrity, and returns reconciliation report. Client accepts conflict responses and surfaces UI. (3 sprints)
- Phase 2 (ops and scale): retention policies, KMS encryption support, telemetry gating, SDK stable APIs, sample UI components for diffs. (4 sprints)

Acceptance criteria (PRD-lite):
- Snapshot size median < 60KB for mobile sample set.
- Server can validate and ingest compact snapshot under 50ms p95 for typical frames (n=5 frames).
- Reconciliation protocol handles mismatch in tool canonical-result-hash with clear conflict codes documented.
- SDK export/import APIs covered by unit tests and sample integration in host SDK repo.

Non-functional/observability checklist:
- Add tracing hooks with snapshot_id correlation.
- Surface per-route snapshot metrics in Console: snapshot_rate, average_size, conflict_rate, replay_success_rate.
- Alert when conflict_rate > 5% for a given customer route.

Next steps / immediate todo (notes to self):
- Draft minimal server resume API spec and post in /product/hosted-api slack thread. (JIRA ticket JIRA-HAPI-1428)
- Sync with Applied ML to define heuristic for checkpoint stability (Ethan).
- Propose canonicalization library with eng infra for tool authors (Marco).
- Run a small mobile field study (10 power users) to measure snapshot sizes on real sessions.

References and related docs:
- see linked artifacts at top
- related internal notes: hosted-api-session-snapshot-onramp-proposal-wip.json, resumable-partial-response-and-sdk-patterns-prd-draft.json (background overlap)

Unresolved design decisions to flag for review meeting:
- Default TTL and adjustable per-route TTL semantics.
- Whether the platform should attempt automated tool re-execution on mismatch (risk of side-effects) or always require explicit developer opt-in.
- Exact snapshot schema (v1) field names — keep compact but readable.

Status: draft -> needs product + eng alignment.

End of doc.
